[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | As God alone creates, He alone provides sustenance.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Truth is a divine name: God exists, possesses truth, and makes truth actual; for creatures, truth is good action, sound belief, and permissible speech.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Conjecture favors one judgment without certainty; it is defective regarding God, while certainty about one’s own future is also defective.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | A servant should not presume to know his own unseen future, but should have certainty about God; the Prophet and his followers are told to call with insight. | mentions 12:108
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The heedless grow blinder the more they hear the Qur’an, while people of spiritual realization grow in guidance; God’s address confuses some and enlightens others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Bodily provision is obedience granted to some and failures granted to others; spiritual provision is connection for some, heedlessness and later punishment or respite for others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | For the spirits, provision means realities of intimacy for some, but worldly heedlessness and eventual punishment or respite for others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God’s control of hearing and sight means He perfects some people’s vision through monotheism and blinds others to realization.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living means bringing a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Although they answer God, they speak from conjecture and words without inward conviction.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | All created things and events are subject to divine will, decree, and power; the decree has already passed and cannot be altered.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Causes cannot alter what is eternal or reverse God’s decree.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | He rejects both assigning partners in creation under the doctrine of predestination and denying God’s power to resurrect; both are unbelief.

[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Managing affairs means directing the whole world, stated generally after specific examples.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | ‘Will you not fear?’ means protect yourselves from punishment for your misguidance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The questions are a rebuke and proof with no escape: God provides rain from heaven and growth from earth, owns hearing and sight, brings life from death and death from life, and governs all affairs.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Examples of bringing the living from the dead include an embryo from semen, bird from egg, and growing plant from earth; the reverse includes egg from bird, while divine governance proceeds through complete, eternal knowledge rather than thought or change.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | They have no answer but God; once they admit His power, the rebuke asks why they do not fear Him instead of treating idols as gods.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | God provides rain from heaven and plants from earth; He created hearing and sight and brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, as previously discussed at 3:27. | mentions 3:27

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | After exposing idol worship, God confronts them with undeniable evidence: provision, hearing and sight, life and death, and governance of all things.

[BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · علي رضي الله عنه | reports | Ali marvels that God made people see through fat, hear through bone, and speak through flesh.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The questioning moves from the obvious gifts people experience to the prior origin of creation: living beings emerge from dead matter and dead matter from living beings.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The life/death contrast covers animals and plants as well as a sperm drop and its products, moving from deficiency to completion.

[ITQAN:v2p564/r3] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Hearing is singular because it is verbal-noun-like and its object, sound, is one kind; sight is plural because it names an organ whose objects—colors and forms—are diverse.
[ITQAN:v3p192#2/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Conjoining a general category after a particular item broadens the statement, while naming the particular first emphasizes its importance; al-Suyuti rejects denial that this construction exists.
[ITQAN:v3p192#2/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari treats ومن يدبر الأمر after the questions about provision as an example of conjoining a general matter after a particular one.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The questions challenge the polytheists to acknowledge God's exclusive right to divinity. Provision comes from heavenly causes such as rain and sun and earthly materials; the earth receives what the sky provides.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Some mystics claim the cosmic pole manages the world and holds up the sky; they may answer that it acts by God's permission, and use المدبرات أمرا for a non-divine manager. | mentions 79:5
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | For من السماء والأرض, من may mark origin; alternatives take it as explanatory after an ellipsis or partitive after an implied إضافة, meaning provisions from the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The disconnected أم introduces a transition, not a correction, and asks who creates and forms hearing and sight, protects them from injury, or controls their persistence and loss; الملك is figurative in these readings.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | The reading of ملك السمع والأبصار as creating them best matches the sequence pairing creative power with provision, as in the cited question about any creator who provides. | mentions 35:3
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The living brought from the dead can mean an animal from a drop and a drop from an animal, or bringing life from death and death from life; interpreting the pair as believer and unbeliever is also reported, while the first explanation is preferred.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Managing the affair generalizes beyond the specific visible matters just listed and signals that all affairs originate with God and return to Him, although humans cannot know their full details.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The polytheists answer Allah without hesitation because the evidence is too plain for denial; الله is the subject with an omitted predicate meaning that God alone performs these acts.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | The verse does not explicitly call God one of the inhabitants of heaven and earth; although texts say He is in heaven in a manner befitting Him, there is no need to change من from its origin sense.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p110/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · صاحب الإنتصاف | reports | He reads the verse as refuting the Qadariyyah claim that God provides only lawful sustenance while people provide themselves with forbidden sustenance, exposing that claim as hidden associationism.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Some argue that the pole and God differ only in consideration because the pole has attained perfect nearness; critics say this collapses into unity of being, which most theologians and some Sufis, including al-Imām al-Rabbānī, reject.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The proposed analogy between a pole and the angels or Jesus managing by God's permission fails: the question asks for the ultimate source to which management returns, so the polytheists can only answer God.
[ALUSI-FULL:v11p111/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | In أفلا تتقون, the interrogative rebukes the actual failure to fear, with the connective following an implied premise: you know this, yet do not fear; the omitted object is God's punishment.

[ELMALILI:10:31/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | God supplies provisions from heaven and earth and owns, creates, equips, governs, and controls hearing and sight, the most noble faculties and means of using provision.
